name: Lake Talquin
type: Ochlockonee River reservoir: stumps, channels and drop-offs, little grass
pool: Averages 15 ft, about 40 ft at the deepest;Jackson Bluff Dam holds the level
notes: Coolest water. Bass stage near the spawning flats; specks school offshore.
Spawn starts on warm spells. Big bass move shallow around the moon.
Peak spawn for bass and specks around the full moon.
Post-spawn. Shellcracker spawn on the full moon.
Shad spawn at dawn; bluegill bed on the full moon.
Summer pattern: topwater early, then mats and offshore grass.
Hottest stretch. Fish first light, last light and after storms.
Hottest water. Short bites at dawn and around storms.
Shad move shallow as the nights cool.
Fall feed. Bass school on shad in creeks and canals.
Cold fronts start the speck bite offshore.
Cold fronts. Bass on outside grass; specks school in open water.

lmb.doing: Winter bass sit on stumps and drops along the Ochlockonee channel, like the bend across from Coe Landing (5 to 18 ft) and 20 ft drops near the islands.
how: Plastic worms and Carolina rigs dragged down the drops.
Deep-running crankbaits around stumps; watch for them.
Live shiners or deep crankbaits in the deep channel.

crappie.doing: Talquin is a world-class crappie lake (the state record came from here). In winter, the Little River bends, about 12 ft deep, hold fish.
how: Open holes in the hyacinth and drop a live minnow or small jig.
Troll jigs and minnows along the old river channel.
Keep only fish 10 inches or longer.

fllinesides.doing: Late fall through spring is striper season. In the lake, the deep channel at High Bluff holds winter stripers; the tailwater below Jackson Bluff Dam is the best-known spot.
how: Live shiners or deep crankbaits from Double Creek to the old pier.
Small crankbaits, vibration lures and stick baits.
Below the dam: 3 a day, only one 24 inches or longer.

bream.doing: Slow. Bluegill and shellcracker hold in deeper grass, canals and around docks; warm, sunny afternoons bring them up.
how: Grass shrimp on the bottom next to hydrilla or eelgrass.
Small jig or worm along canal edges and docks.

lmb.doing: Pre-spawn bass move into the back of the Little River arm (12 ft in the channel, 7 to 8 ft on the edges) and onto flats like the Hunter Creek mouth, about 4 ft deep.
how: Plastic crawfish or a 1/4 oz lipless crankbait in the creek.

crappie.doing: January through April is the best crappie fishing of the year. Trolling the deep channels, around 20 ft, is the standard way to find them.
how: Jigs or minnows along the deep channels near 20 ft.
Minnows on stumps and logs along the drops.

fllinesides.doing: White bass run up the upper Ochlockonee in late winter and spring; stripers stay active in the deep channels.
how: Small spinners and jigs in the current.

bream.doing: Shellcracker move onto firm sand and shell near the grass ahead of the spring full moons; bluegill feed around reeds and docks.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom with a split shot.
Crickets or grass shrimp under a small float along reeds.

lmb.doing: Bass bed in pockets and creek backs around the full moon, on hard bottom near cover.
how: Swimbait or Fluke in the backs of pockets first thing.

crappie.doing: Crappie move into the creek arms and shallow wood to spawn. The Little River arm is a spawning area from February through May.
how: Minnow under a float on wood and pads.
Keep trolling the channel edges between waves.

fllinesides.doing: Stripers run upriver to spawn; many hold in the current at river mouths and jetties, feeding on shad.
how: Live shad or shrimp on the bottom in the current.
Small spoons and jigs at fish on top.

bream.doing: Shellcracker bed on the March and April full moons on firm sand and shell near grass. Bluegill start as the water warms.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom; work the area until you find the colony.
Small beetle spin along the edge of the flat.

lmb.doing: Shad spawn on riprap and seawalls at dawn, then bass move to bream beds, docks and the first drop off the bank.
how: Spinnerbait, buzzbait or topwater on riprap and seawalls.
Shaky head skipped into the shade.

crappie.doing: Crappie leave the banks for docks and brush in 10 to 15 ft. Singles and small groups are often the bigger fish.
how: Minnows set just above the brush.

fllinesides.doing: As the lake passes the mid 70s, stripers head for cool spring runs and deep holes; sunshine bass school at dawn.
how: Small topwaters and spoons at schooling fish.
Live bait in spring runs and deep holes.

bream.doing: Shellcracker beds show up on the sandy flats near High Bluff around mid-April and last about three months. Bluegill feed along docks, points and the shoreline.
how: Worms on the bottom, or a small Beetle Spin.
Pitch crickets along docks and points.

lmb.doing: Bass school on shad: around Talquin Flats, along the Little River and at creek mouths. Bigger fish hold on the deep channels.
how: Topwater stick baits such as a Long A.
Deep crankbaits or dark Carolina-rigged worms in the channels.

crappie.doing: Crappie suspend over deep brush and under shaded docks, just above the thermocline. Night fishing under lights is good.
how: Minnows on a mini Carolina rig, set just above the brush.
Cast a small jig from 25 to 30 ft off the brush.
Lights on a deep dock or bridge.

fllinesides.doing: Striper and bass schools feed on shad in the Little River in summer.
how: Small crankbaits, spoons and stick baits at busting fish.

bream.doing: Bluegill keep spawning on each full moon; between moons they hold in deeper pads, grass patches and around docks. Fish early.
how: Grass shrimp in deep pads and hydrilla patches; anchor and chum lightly.
Worms and crickets along the walkways.

lmb.doing: Shad push into creeks and pockets, and bass follow them shallow.
how: Crankbaits, spinnerbaits and topwater around bait in pockets.
Jig or shaky head on wood and docks.

crappie.doing: Crappie are on docks and brush early, then pull off cover into roaming schools in the creeks as the water cools.
how: Shoot jigs under docks with brush or shade.
Cast a jig just past a school and keep it above them.
Bright jigs in clear water, dark after rain.

fllinesides.doing: Cooling water brings stripers back out; schools chase shad around points, pilings and channel edges.
how: Lipless crankbaits, spoons and bucktails at busting fish.
Live shrimp or shad tight to pilings in current.

bream.doing: Bream feed hard in the grass as the water cools. Fewer beds, steady numbers.
how: Anchor near a thick hydrilla patch and fish grass shrimp or worms near the bottom.
Crickets under a cork along reed lines.
